top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks. The magic-wavelength lattice cancels the trap light shift by design for a large neutral-atom ensemble, which is a distinct principle from the frequency comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012). Fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 have been reproduced independently in several national laboratories, so the achievement is mature. The citation scope stays on the invention and the demonstrated performance, without claiming the redefinition of the second. The two-name allocation is a committee judgement, since Lemonde, Lisdat and Ludlow are left out, but it is defensible and better than withholding the prize; no award (P000) is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented link to Katori or Ye, and my own field (superconducting circuits, WACQT, Chalmers) is distant from optical lattice clocks
